newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsang confident HK legislators will pass budget.
newsitem.headline: Tsang confident HK legislators will pass budget.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary said on Thursday he foresaw no problem from Hong Kong's future legislature over his 1997/98 budget.
Tsang unveiled his budgetry plans on Wednesday for the 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal year which covers the handover to Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.
China plans to dissolve Hong Kong's elected legislature when it takes back Hong Kong because it opposes British democratic reforms which governed the 1995 legislative elections.

An interim provisional legislature, expected to sit for about a year, was selected in December by a China-assembled panel to the anger of Hong Kong's pro-democracy lobby which adamantly opposes the move.
The provisional legislature expects to be consulted but member Eric Li described Tsang's budget as sensible.
"There is a lot of room for improvement. But to have a very safe and prudent budget is typical particularly at this sensitive time," he said by telephone.
In his budget speech on Wednesday, Tsang reported a HK$15.1 billion ($1.96 billion) budget surplus and forecast more to come.
But he resisted the temptation to proffer tax cuts angering social activists who argue Hong Kong is now wealthy enough to improve its rudimentary safety net for the disadvantaged.
Tsang said his immediate priority was to get the budget through the existing Legislative Council -- where delegates have added their voices to demands for improved welfare spending.
"It has been a joint enterprise so for that reason I am reasonably confident it will command the support of the Chinese side as well as (Hong Kong's future leader) the Chief Executive."
"So there you are. My priorities as I said are to try to get (the existing) legislature to agree."
